Empirical Research Plan  
“Does increased competition in the banking sector improve credit access and terms for small firms?”

====================================================================
1. Identification Strategy
--------------------------------------------------------------------
Method: Difference-in-Differences (DID) with an event–study extension and an “intensity” treatment.

•  Two dimensions of quasi-random variation  
  – Across states: how restrictive interstate branching rules are (Rice-Strahan index 0–4).  
  – Over time: each state changes its rules only once (or never) between 1994 and 2005.

•  Continuous-treatment DID (“dose–response”) exploits the size of the deregulation, not just a 0/1 switch.  
•  Event-study coefficients (-4,-3,-2,-1, 0, +1 … years relative to first relaxation) allow graphical pre-trend tests.

Why appropriate?  
(i)  All surveys (1993, 1998, 2003) straddle the policy change.  
(ii)  Firms cannot influence state branching laws.  
(iii)  Rich controls and fixed effects are available at the firm, industry, and state level.

====================================================================
2. Treatment and Control
--------------------------------------------------------------------
Treatment variable  
Tist  = (4 – RS_indexst) / 4              rescaled to 0 = most restrictive, 1 = fully open.

•  “Intensive” treatment = increase in Tist between survey waves.  
•  Binary variant for robustness: 1 = state ever drops index by ≥2 points by year t.

Control group  
Firms in states that did not loosen restrictions (ΔTist = 0) during the same window.

Treatment timing  
Event date for state s = year the first of the four restrictions is removed (FDIC enactment file).  
For DID we code Postst = 1 if survey-year t ≥ event-year of state s.

Running variable / cutoff – Not applicable (not an RDD).

====================================================================
3. Key Identifying Assumptions
--------------------------------------------------------------------
A1. Parallel trends: Absent deregulation, credit outcomes of firms in more- vs. less-restrictive states would have followed the same trend.  
Plausibility: No obvious pre-1994 divergence; can be checked with 1993 pre-period and event-study leads.

A2. No simultaneous, differential credit-market shocks correlated with branching laws.  
Plausibility: Major federal programs (e.g., SBA, CRA reforms) were nationwide; include state-year HHI and macro controls.

A3. Stable unit treatment value (no cross-state spillovers).  
Plausibility: Some interstate lending may cross borders; we drop firms within 50 miles of a state border in robustness.

A4. Survey composition stability: Changes in who is sampled do not mechanically line up with treatment.  
Plausibility: SSBF uses uniform sampling weights; we re-weight and show balanced observable characteristics.

====================================================================
4. Threats to Identification & Mitigations
--------------------------------------------------------------------
T1. Endogenous policy choice (states deregulate when small-firm credit demand rises).  
  – Mitigation: control for lagged state-level small-business loan growth, legislators’ ideology, and include state-specific linear trends.  
  – Instrumental-variables robustness: instrument ΔTist with pre-1994 bank-lobby contribution intensity and partisan control.

T2. Differential macro shocks (energy states, tech boom states).  
  – Mitigation: industry-year FE, state-year unemployment & GDP controls; cluster SEs two-way (state, year).

T3. Measurement error in Rice-Strahan index.  
  – Mitigation: use alternative binary treatment “Has state deposit cap?”; show results consistent.

====================================================================
5. R Code Outline
--------------------------------------------------------------------
```r
#-----------------------------#
# 0.  Packages
#-----------------------------#
library(data.table)   # fast data work
library(fixest)       # high-dim FE
library(did)          # Sun & Abraham
library(ggplot2)

#-----------------------------#
# 1.  Load data
#-----------------------------#
ssbf93 <- fread("SSBF_1993.csv")
ssbf98 <- fread("SSBF_1998.csv")
ssbf03 <- fread("SSBF_2003.csv")
rs      <- fread("rice_strahan_index_1990_2005.csv")   # state-year
concen  <- fread("fdic_hhi_stateyear.csv")             # state-year HHI

# Harmonise survey waves
ssbf <- rbindlist(list(ssbf93, ssbf98, ssbf03), fill = TRUE)
ssbf[, survey_year := year]           # harmonised

#-----------------------------#
# 2.  Merge policy variables
#-----------------------------#
ssbf <- merge(ssbf, rs,    by = c("state","survey_year"))
ssbf <- merge(ssbf, concen,by = c("state","survey_year"), all.x = TRUE)

# Treatment intensity
ssbf[, treat_intensity := (4 - rs_index)/4]            # 0–1

# Event time: years since first deregulation
event_years <- rs[, .(event_year = min(year[rs_index < shift(rs_index, fill = 4)])), by = state]
ssbf <- merge(ssbf, event_years, by = "state", all.x = TRUE)
ssbf[, rel_year := survey_year - event_year]

#-----------------------------#
# 3.  Outcomes
#-----------------------------#
ssbf[, rate_spread := loan_rate - prime_rate]          # example outcome
# Additional outcomes: collateral dummy, credit-line indicator, loan size, etc.

#-----------------------------#
# 4.  Main DID specification
#-----------------------------#
fe_spec <- feols(rate_spread ~ treat_intensity*post + firm_size + firm_age +
                   credit_score + owner_demog + hhi +
                   i(industry, survey_year) | state + survey_year,
                 data = ssbf, weights = ~weight, cluster = ~state)

summary(fe_spec)

#-----------------------------#
# 5.  Event-study (Sun & Abraham)
#-----------------------------#
es <- att_gt(yname = "rate_spread",
             gname = "event_year",
             idname = "firm_id",
             tname = "survey_year",
             xformla = ~ firm_size + credit_score,
             data = ssbf,
             est_method = "dr")

ggdid(es) + theme_bw()

#-----------------------------#
# 6.  Robustness: drop border firms
#-----------------------------#
ssbf_rb <- ssbf[border_distance > 50]
fe_spec_rb <- update(fe_spec, data = ssbf_rb)
etable(list(Main = fe_spec, NoBorder = fe_spec_rb))
```

====================================================================
6. Expected Results
--------------------------------------------------------------------
Theory: Greater bank competition lowers lending spreads and relaxes collateral/guarantee requirements.

Prior sign & ballpark: 25–40 bp reduction in interest-rate spread for a one-point drop (25 pct-pt increase in openness). Collateral probability expected to fall by ~5 ppt; credit-line limit expected to rise by ~8 %.

====================================================================
7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment
--------------------------------------------------------------------
(Example checklist for DID)  
C1 — Common-trend evidence (pre-period parallel) …………… 1  
C2 — No anticipatory behavior detected in leads ……………… 1  
C3 — No spillovers/SUTVA plausibly holds …………………… 0.5  
C4 — Correct treatment timing and stable assignment ……… 1  
C5 — Robust to alternative specs / placebo outcomes ……… 1  

Total ≈ 4.5 / 5 → strong but not perfect identification.
